name: Medial Taylor and Scham approach to the coronoid
aliases: Taylor and Scham flexor-pronator reflecting approach
corridor: Medial approach reflecting the whole flexor-pronator mass extraperiosteally from posterior to anterior off the ulna to expose the coronoid base while preserving the medial collateral ligament

positioning.text: Position supine with the arm on a hand table and the medial elbow accessible.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the medial epicondyle, the crest of the ulnar shaft, the olecranon, and the sublime tubercle.

incision.text: Use a posterior incision with a medial flap or a direct medial incision, protecting the posterior branches of the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve.

superficial_interval.text: Identify and protect the ulnar nerve, unroofing it about 6 cm proximal and distal to the epicondyle starting proximally, and incise the fascia between the FCU heads while protecting the first motor branch.

deep_interval.text: Elevate the flexor carpi ulnaris and the whole flexor-pronator mass extraperiosteally from posterior to anterior, starting at the ulnar crest and the flat olecranon surface, to expose the coronoid fracture base, dissecting distal to proximal toward the sublime tubercle to protect the medial collateral ligament.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve, the ulnar nerve, the flexor-pronator mass, and the medial coronoid base.

structures_at_risk.text: The ulnar nerve and the medial collateral ligament are the primary structures at risk.

danger_zones.text: The sublime tubercle region is the danger zone for the medial collateral ligament during elevation.

retraction_hazards.text: Stay strictly extraperiosteal and dissect distal to proximal toward the sublime tubercle to keep the medial collateral ligament intact, and protect the ulnar nerve.

exposure.text: Exposes the base of the coronoid for medial plate fixation.

limitations.text: It is designed for large basilar coronoid fractures; an over-the-top interval is added if anterior capsule access is needed.

indications.text: Indicated for medial plate fixation of large, basilar coronoid fractures.

closure.text: Reattach the flexor-pronator mass, ensure the ulnar nerve lies in a healthy bed, and close in layers.

complications.text: Complications include ulnar neuropathy, medial collateral ligament insufficiency, and flexor-pronator weakness.

procedure_applications.condition: A large basilar coronoid fracture needs medial plate fixation

questions.question: What is the crucial pearl of the Taylor and Scham approach?
questions.answer: Preserve the medial collateral ligament by dissecting distal to proximal toward the sublime tubercle and staying extraperiosteal.

questions.question: In which direction is the flexor-pronator mass elevated?
questions.answer: Extraperiosteally from posterior to anterior, starting at the ulnar crest.

questions.question: What is the main indication for this approach?
questions.answer: Medial plate fixation of large basilar coronoid fractures.
